projects.title: Show HN: Selbstbild – What Fable 5 thinks of your HN comment history
projects.author: Topfi
projects.summary: Like everyone on HN, I love nothing more than to (re)read my own comments. Getting my intuition that I am among the smartest, most humble, highest quality commenters on here confirmed by an LLM so capable that the US government had to temporarily export restrict it [0] seemed only natural. Having had my perfection confirmed, I decided to share this joy with you as I had a few percent usage left before a reset. I took a few prompts, then did a review of the output which resulted in Selbstbild, a BYOK (Anthropic / OpenRouter) web app that gives you a summary and assessment of your public comments by one of our machine Gods, including Fable 5 (provided your can afford that luxury at API pricing). In all seriousness, I have, for a long time, used my own comments on social media (including HN) as part of a personal needle-in-haystack test, simply because I do know my somewhat peculiar style and what I tend to write, but also because I can sometimes write in a slightly confusing manner, making for a decently quick check during a models release window. Lately though, what with long context retrieval at the frontier having become rather robust, the interesting part has become not whether but how a model sifts through this unstructured collection of comments, what is surfaced in which manner, etc. Hence this. * Everything runs in your browser, the only network calls go to Anthropic / OpenRouter and the platform APIs, nothing is proxied through a server, no analytics, no cookies. Feel free to verify via the network tab and source code, I would. * You get a cost estimate before any tokens are spent, so no surprises there. * Caveats: LLMs are not intelligent entities, have no predictive abilities and this is not a tool for professional assessment of your person. This is a horoscope for nerds. * Creation: Fable built essentially all of this itself, my own contribution was a few minutes of prompting, plus review and deployment. * No cookie banner: Turns out you aren’t actually “forced” to display one, just if you are doing something that, in my opinion, users should really be aware of you doing do you actually need one. * Classifier: Depending on your topic, your comments may trigger the Fable 5 classifier. Nothing I can do about this, but it’s transparently communicated. For what it’s worth, my comments did not trigger it. On the state of LLM coding as a whole: My review found a few issues. Deleting from Cloudflare KV did not account for cache initially, so that could lead to content being retained even when users requested deletion, which isn’t ideal. Also, a few “any” snuck in and Fable 5 decided on an ancient version of the Anthropic API. Was caught via a quick read of the code, which is overall as pleasant to review as can be (certainly prefer reviewing Anthropic model output over GPT-5.5 purely from a subjective standpoint) but if such obvious deficiencies can sneak in on such a simple project with such an advanced model, that tells me we are still far from a stage where “no review” is even something we can discuss. These issues would have likely been caught by a second review pass anyways (whether using a review agent, prompting Fable or another model), but it still gives me pause what other issues could sneak in as part of more important and complex code bases. Get yourself assessed by Fable 5: https://selbstbild.eu Repo: https://github.com/Topfi/selbstbild [0] https://www.anthropic.com/news/fable-mythos-access

projects.summary: 在线浏览： （点「🧩 Skills」，支持搜索和分类筛选） Skills（AI 技能包）最近很热，但资源基本都是英文的：anthropics/skills（16.6万⭐）、awesome-claude-skills（7.1万⭐）、agent-skills（8.1万⭐）—— 中文用户既看不懂说明，也不知道有哪些中文 skill 可用。 于是整理了这个合集： 87 个 Skill，其中 30 个中文原创 中文这部分是最有价值的，全是中文场景刚需，但散落各处没人整理过： 去 AI 味改写 —— 说人话（⭐928）、繁中版 speak-human-tw（⭐744） 学术写作 —— 学术科研三件套（⭐2556）、中文论文排版、学术降 AIGC 检测 自媒体 —— 小红书运营 139 个技能（⭐346）、公众号一键排版发布（⭐679） 求职 —— JobOK 求职全流程、Auto-CV 简历自动生成 其他 —— superpowers 中文版（⭐7458，26万⭐框架完整汉化）、鱼皮编程技能包、法言法语、技术写作 几个可能有用的点 1. 每个仓库都调 GitHub API 验证过真实存在（原始清单里有 404 的已剔除），星数是实测数据 2. 纠正了一个流传的错误：多个高星英文仓库写的安装路径是 ~/.config/claude-code/skills/，但实测 macOS 上实际生效的是 ~/.claude/skills/ —— 抄来抄去没人验证 3. 也整理了 npx skills add <仓库地址> 这个一键安装方式 4. 中英对照说明，官方 skill 的中文说明译自各 SKILL.md 的 description 原文 站点本身是一个 AI 工具导航（47 个工具，标注免费额度，链接每天自动检测），Skills 是新增的板块。纯静态、无广告、无跟踪。 信息有误欢迎指出，我会尽快改。

projects.summary: 🧩 Interactive Concepts — 动态交互式概念可视化 概念 Interactive Concepts 是一个面向教育、科研和创作者的可视化工具：它能把抽象的文字说明转化为 交互式图表与概念演示。 目标不是静态插图，而是提供一种 可以点击、拖动、探索的动态概念体验，让复杂知识更直观。 网站入口：Interactive Concepts 为什么做这个 传统的静态图表或科研插图虽然能表达结构，但缺乏交互性。 而在课堂、科研展示或社交分享中，用户往往希望能 直接操作和探索概念： “能不能把 DNA 结构做成可旋转的图？” “我想让学生点击不同层次，看到对应的解释。” “能不能做一个交互式的流程演示，而不是死板的 PPT？” Interactive Concepts 把这个流程产品化，避免用户自己写复杂的代码或交互脚本。 能做什么 交互式图表生成：输入文字 → 输出可点击、可拖动的概念图 动态演示：支持课堂演示、科研讲解、社交分享 多层次探索：用户可展开、折叠、切换不同层次信息 跨平台分享：嵌入网页、教学平台或社交媒体 交互式学习：适合教师、学生和科研人员的知识传播 有什么不同 大多数可视化工具只提供静态导出，而 Interactive Concepts 刻意做得很窄： 它的目标不是生成任意图片，而是 交互式的知识演示。 产品重点： 动态交互体验 多层次信息结构 教学与科研场景优化 跨平台嵌入与分享 直观的用户操作 安全边界 Interactive Concepts 明确定位为 教育与科研辅助工具，而非官方出版物或权威教材。 产品设计上避免： 误导性科学结论 未经验证的实验数据 官方教材的直接复制 商业或品牌化的过度包装 适合谁 教师：想做课堂演示 科研人员：需要动态展示复杂概念 学生：想要更直观的学习体验 创作者：想在社交媒体上分享知识内容 使用场景 把抽象的 科学概念 转化为交互式图表 在课堂上做 动态演示，让学生点击探索 在科研报告中嵌入 交互式流程图 在社交平台上分享 可操作的知识内容 不写代码，也能做一个 交互式教学图表

projects.title: Show HN: I built custom movie dashboards for Apple TV
projects.author: zacksiri
projects.summary: At home we have Netflix, Disney+, Amazon Prime Video, HBO Max, and Apple TV+, but somehow we still end up just scrolling around, giving up, and watching YouTube. There must be over 10,000 movies across these streaming platforms, so it is not a lack of content. It is the pain of having to go through each app, search separately, and look at recommendations that do not really interest me. So I built Memovee, where I can search across my streaming apps with prompts like: - “Top 90s action movies on Netflix” - “Adventure movies I can watch with my kids” - “Find me some movies with great music I must watch”" I can then save those movies to a list, add the list to a dashboard, and use that dashboard on Apple TV to quickly jump into the right streaming app. Memovee brings the focus back to movies, rather than the apps themselves. I wanted more control over what comes into my living room, and what my kids watch, instead of just accepting whatever the streaming platforms want to promote at that moment. Now I can make dashboards for family movie nights, dashboard for my kids, something for myself or a date night with my wife. Memovee is available as a Web / iOS / Apple TV App. App Store: https://links.memovee.com/aB1x/p6157asv I'd love to hear your feedback.

projects.summary: Hey HN, sharing my new app here - Clinch. I decided to make this app while going through the layoff time at GitLab, though I am safe. During the time, I was bit anxious and offcourse did not have lot of work to do, I doomscroll a lot and hence my mental and phone usage hit badly. I decided to put this time to work on some side project and came up with the idea to kill my existing pattern. I tried One Sec, got numb to the same breath, and wanted something that stayed novel and made me notice the pattern. When you open an app you've chosen, Clinch steps in with a short (~10–30s) moment — a breath, a spot-the-dot game, a fact, a finger labyrinth — then asks one question: "what brought you here?" It rotates through 6 moment types so your brain can't autopilot through a repeated ritual. It's been 2 weeks since I published the app and so far got 25 downloads. I realised that distribution is more tougher now. Sharing to the community here if you wanted to try out and have some suggestion on the app or distribution. projects.title: Show HN: Riley – Content That Sounds Like You, Not Like AI
projects.author: vacostacambas
projects.summary: Working for a US company with several, very different, lines of business taught me how difficult it is to post on social media consistently and keeping the essence of each brand in all posts. Standard AI tools helped me get the first draft, but that was it. I would spend hours editing the output to make it sound a bit more like me, but in the end this was more time-consuming than starting from a blank page. Tired of choosing between consistency and maintaining the brand’s essence and my voice, I built Riley. My goal was to teach AI how I sound and the essence of each brand to remove endless prompts and constant tweaking, keep creative momentum, and make content creation a smooth and enjoyable process. Riley learns from previous content you’ve written to generate pieces that sounds like you, not like AI. You can import examples (LinkedIn posts, website copy, social media, etc.), define context with @context-pills for background, audience, and style, and refine with feedback and comments. With one-line prompts, Riley outputs tailored pieces for multiple platforms at once while adapting over time. The more you teach Riley with feedback, the better she’ll write. Riley learns your style by extracting patterns from your imported writing and ongoing edits/comments, such as vocabulary, sentence rhythm, tone preferences, structures, and what to avoid. No need to actually explain to her “how you write,” she will know the more you work with her. This becomes persistent context that informs every generation, rather than one-off instructions. How is Riley different from ChatGPT or Claude? Standard LLMs require repeating lengthy context in every new session, and if you ask the model to create several pieces at once, the LLM will most likely write 2-3 really good pieces, and then start creating content you wish the LLM had never written. Looking for feedback about (1) onboarding flow, (2) platform UX/UI, (3) how well Riley preserves nuances of personal/brand voice, (4) features you’d like to see in Riley, (5) anything else you can think of. projects.title: Show HN: Clockjumper – An Intervibed Project
projects.author: HaphazardGuess
projects.summary: Hello there, Long time listener, first time caller over here. I’ve been meaning to try A.I coding capabilities for some time now. I wanted to focus on a problem that is simple enough for me to execute all the way to the finish line. I didn’t want to mess with any backend complexities or deal with a website that requires APIs or some such. I figured a simple timezone conversion tool would be a decent choice. It is a solved problem to the point of becoming a commodity and all I’m doing is adding, subtracting time and making some tweaks here and there. I don’t know if someone out there has already coined a term for this workflow of mine but I’m claiming a stake and naming it “an Intervibed project”. I’ve used multiple different A.Is to code everything and I can assure you that I’m actively suffering from “Prompt Fatigue”…….so what about this one? has this term been coined yet? I damn sure hope so! The project is being hosted on Lovable, I run my initial prompts thru chatgpt 5.5 Pro and then submit the results to Claude Opus 4.8 Max and then I submit the final execution order to Lovable. I initially used Lovable’s own design capabilities to do the UX/UI but when Claude released the design feature I ran the whole through that and I’m using a new design now. As for SEO/GEO, I created this project six months ago and at that time the Lovable websites were not getting crawled by search engines. After the recent Lovable update, they have pretty much solved that issue (or so I’ve been told?). I recreated the project on the new tech stack and I have no issues with Google Search Console crawling and indexing. I’m also promoting this website on Facebook and once again I’m using a similar workflow to create….or rather generate posts for socials….I’m very curious to see how and when will the artwork start to drift. I have locked down a “master spec” for every asset but still every time I generate something new from my existing assets it looks a bit off. It’s definitely been quite an experience and I’ve learned a ton about how these A.I products approach a problem, their limitations, strengths. All of this can become a write up on its own in the future and It’s a gonna be a one long rant guaranteed. I feel like I can make some unbelievably basic UX/UI and productivity recommendations to the product managers in charge of these multizillion dollar companies. A.I is supposed to save us time and effort and it sure does, but the actual mechanics of using the A.I tools is still residing in the stoneage…is “A.I Stoneage” a term yet? It should be. I will give you one example, why am I not able to collapse specific prompts responses inside a chat? Why am I not allowed to delete a specific response within a long chat? This is simple stuff folks, forums were doing these things back when dinosaurs roamed the earth….I remember very clearly….anyways. I would like for you all to take this lil’ website of mine for a test drive and tell me what do you think. Your positive feedback will encourage me to keep on going and the negative’s ones will help me do a better job. Boy oh boy I do want to be doing a better job. Keep in my mind that this is just a fun side project that I spend 2,3 hours a week on and it’s all been done in good fun! Thanks much, P

projects.title: Show HN: Afair – Self-organizing memory shared across your AI tools
projects.author: izax
projects.summary: afair has been the one tool I can't work without for months, and I just open-sourced it. It gives every AI you use one shared memory that stays yours. Where it comes from: I use a different AI for almost everything now, building projects, researching health questions, whatever's in front of me, and I switch harnesses constantly (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Claude.ai). None of them share anything, so I kept re-explaining myself from scratch every session. afair is the fix: a memory layer that lives in a vault you own and connects to every tool over MCP. Tell one, the rest know. The part I went deep on is that it structures itself. Every AI has memory now, but almost all of it just stores what you say and pulls it back later. afair keeps going: a set of background ("cold-path") agents read your activity and derive the shape of it, extract entities, build an entity graph, score salience, resolve conflicts, consolidate what matters, and let the rest decay, roughly the way memory works in a brain. You never file or tag anything. Underneath, the substrate is append-only and content-addressed (SQLite + FTS5 + sqlite-vec, encrypted), so nothing is ever rewritten. New interpretations are versioned views over the same immutable log, so you can always re-derive them. It runs single-tenant (your own instance), you can export everything on demand, and it exposes three frozen MCP verbs: remember / recall / observe. AGPLv3, built in Germany. It's vendor-neutral through litellm, so it works with any model. If you already pay for GitHub Copilot you can use that as the model with no separate API key. Local setup is about two minutes: clone, uv sync, uv run python -m afair, point your MCP client at localhost. There's a one-command installer for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, Windsurf and others, plus a one-line instruction snippet for CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md so your tools reach for it on their own. It's early and not perfect. The honest hard part is keeping the interpreted layer trustworthy as it grows: sharper retrieval, the entity graph, conflict resolution, the cold-path agents. If that's your kind of problem the code is right there. I'd love feedback, and I'll actually read and review PRs. Repo: https://github.com/afairai/afair

projects.title: Show HN: Quxnet
projects.author: replwoacause
projects.summary: TLDR: I miss the genuine human connection I used to get from the internet, and I’ve grown weary of all the modern social media BS. I wrote more in depth about my inspiration for making this here: https://quxnet.net/about . quxnet is more of an art project than anything. My latest passion project is building a network around the idea of the old web. I took inspiration from systems like BBSes, Usenet, pubnix hosts, and especially early internet message boards. The UI is less BBS and more forum based, I’d say. The inspiration from BBSes, Usenet, etc. is mostly philosophical. The UI's pretty plain but that's the way I like it, and it's focused on text content. I named it quxnet (pronounced "kwucks") because "qux" is a metasyntactic variable in programming and I liked it. I also thought it was kind of funny. It has sealed mail, boards, docs, profiles with log entries and status lines, picons (user profile images that get dithered by the network on upload), a links directory with random browsing in the spirit of StumbleUpon, an RSS reader, and pages that let you put a website online for free at `yourhandle.quxnet.pub`. I even added a dialer on login if you want a little nostalgia hit and don’t mind the gimmick. It can be disabled in settings if you do. Oh, and it’s scriptable, has a macro system and API, and exporting your data is a first-class feature. The tech stack is simple. It’s all SSR, written in a programming language I’ve been working on since the pandemic. Well, it’s actually more than a language, but that’s outside the scope of this post. The DB is SQLite, backing up with Litestream to Cloudflare R2. All of this runs on an $8 Hetzner VPS, which handles it just fine. Last thing I’ll say is, the hardest part about all of this hasn’t been the software. I’m sure those of you with experience launching things already know this. The hard part is getting people to participate. Funny how this still applies even to something free xD We have a nice little cohort of folks on there now, with some interesting threads forming around IBM 360/135 mainframes running DOS/VS, early personal computer collections (Sinclair ZX80, ZX Spectrum, BBC Micro, Atari ST), riding motorcycles, drinking kava, and talking philosophy. We have some musicians and authors. A mix of young and old it seems. We have a few old school BBS operators and some of the younger posters are talking about their dumbphones and running DOSBox, VICE, and WinUAE to run old demos from the demoscene. It’s fun seeing real, meaningful conversations unfold but overcoming the cold start is harder than I expected. :/ If any of this sounds like your bag, you should drop by. I know HN hates signing up for things just to try them. I really grappled with this before posting, but in this case, I’d argue that’s one of the value props of a network like this. I strongly considered adding a guest mode to make looking around easier, but was worried it would violate the trust contract with the community. Instead I opened registration and temporarily removed the invite requirement to bring the friction down a bit. I know I'll probably get less feedback as a result but it's the only way I could think to do it without pulling a bait and switch on the existing members. There’s nothing for sale here, so hopefully that offsets some of the irk of having to give an email. Just use a throwaway or Proton address. :] Hope to see you on the boards. -- sysop

projects.title: 【开源自荐】self-media-compliance-review：自媒体内容发布前的合规风险审核 Skill
projects.author: JuneYaooo
projects.summary: 最近开始做自媒体，发现一个挺常见但又很难排查的问题：内容有时候不知道为什么就违规了。 有些问题在官方规则里能找到依据，但更多时候，只有等到被限流、下架、提示违规，或者申诉失败之后，才慢慢从别人的经验里知道可能踩了什么点。 所以我整理了一个开源的 Agent Skill： 它主要做两件事。 第一，收录各个平台的官方规则说明，目前包括视频号、微信公众号、抖音、快手、B站、小红书等平台。 第二，整理社交媒体上创作者讨论过的违规案例、申诉经验、评论回复和一些疑似“隐形规则”的线索。官方规则是主要依据，创作者讨论只作为辅助参考，用来帮助排查那些规则没有写得很细、但实际发布时经常遇到的问题。 使用时，可以让支持 Skills 的 AI Agent 帮忙做违规答疑，或者在内容发布前做一遍风险检查。比如检查标题、封面、字幕、口播、商品链接、发布文案里有没有比较明显的风险点。 这个项目不是法律意见，也不能保证平台一定审核通过。它更像是一个发布前的自查清单和经验库，帮助自己在发布前多看一遍，也希望能帮助大家更好、更安全地做自媒体。 开源出来也是想邀请大家一起补充：各个平台的新规则、真实踩坑案例、申诉经验、整改方式，以及哪些说法容易被误判。

projects.title: Show HN: Curvytron 2, I rewrote my browser party game, 10 years later
projects.author: tom32i
projects.summary: Hi everyone, french web dev here, About 10 years ago I did a little party game in the browser inspired by Achtung die Kurve genre, it reached HN ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=9494619 ) and everything went crazy, it's still largely played in open-spaces all over the world today. This past year, I've been working on a sequel: https://curvytron2.com is live. Same goal as the first one: challenge myself, perfect my skills, have fun and give back to the internet community the best way I know; by just putting a free little fun game out there. No ads, no tracking, no business plan. A decade of professional web development and hours of GMTK have raised my expectations and this time I aimed for: - a good looking top-down 3D view with improved gameplay and real game juice: I learn Three.JS and WebGL for this project, worked on the camera movements, screen shake, sound design, gameplay feedback and I'm proud of the portal-like effect of the bonus that allows you to peak and cross over to the other side of the map. - a solid 100fps server simulation (in Go) serving clients with a really bandwidth efficient netcode (it's binary websocket instead of plain JSON and I open-sourced it: https://github.com/Tom32i/netcode ). - Instant reconnection, at any time: I had this requirement from day one, in the first curvytron losing connexion meant dropping out of the game permanently. Not anymore. You can just refresh the page mid-game and keep playing, try it yourself. The game runs in any desktop and mobile browser and supports gamepads I've put up servers in US and Europe to offer a good ping to as much players as I can afford at the moment. I still maintain and host the first game to keep the original experience live. I'd love to get feedback from HN, and don't hesitate to stress-test the game of course! I'll be around to answer questions and discuss if you're interested. Cheers!

projects.title: [开源推荐] TeamoRouter — LLM API 路由网关：Claude Code / Codex 国内使用与 ccswitch 迁移完整指南
projects.author: blammectrappora
projects.summary: TeamoRouter 是一个 LLM API 路由网关，主要解决国内开发者使用 Claude Code、Codex CLI、Codex Desktop 时的 API 接入问题。 当前国内 AI 开发者的痛点： 1. 直接注册 Anthropic/OpenAI → 需要海外信用卡，绑卡容易被拒，账号容易被封 2. 用公共中转 API → 延迟不稳定，Agent 协议（Tool Use、Streaming、MCP）经常被阉割 3. 自建代理/VPN → 配置复杂，换模型要重新配 TeamoRouter 在中间加了一层 API 路由层，把这些问题封装到底层： 你的代码 → TeamoRouter API → 官方模型（Claude / GPT） ├─ 自动路由 ├─ 协议适配 ├─ 负载均衡 └─ 国内网络优化 ccswitch 用户迁移： bash 原来用 ccswitch export ANTHROPICBASEURL= 换到 TeamoRouter（只需改一个 URL） export ANTHROPICBASEURL= export ANTHROPICAPIKEY=tr-xxxxxxxx 然后正常用 claude 命令即可 claude "帮我写一个 Python 脚本" Codex CLI 用户： bash export CODEXBASEURL= export CODEXAPIKEY=tr-xxxxxxxx codex Codex Desktop 用户： 下载 Teamo Switch 桌面端（macOS/Windows），一键安装 Codex Desktop + 配置路由，不需要手动配环境变量。 项目亮点 1. ccswitch 无缝替代 — 同样的环境变量接入方式，零迁移成本 2. 完整 Agent 协议 — Tool Use、Streaming、MCP、Beta Features 全部原生支持，不是阉割版 3. 国内网络优化 — 多 region 智能路由，低延迟，无需 VPN 4. 多模型统一接入 — 一个 Key 调 Claude、GPT 等多个模型 5. 价格透明 — 按量后付费，约官方 10% 起，无月费，支持国内支付 相关信息

projects.summary: TeamoRouter：LLM API 路由网关 背景 国内开发者用 Claude Code、Codex 做 AI 编程时，最头疼的几个问题： 1. 账号难注册 — Anthropic/OpenAI 需要海外信用卡，绑卡经常被拒 2. 容易被封号 — IP 不干净或支付信息被标记，账号说没就没了 3. 中转不稳定 — 公共中转 API 延迟忽高忽低，Agent 协议经常缺功能 4. 配置复杂 — 换个模型还得换 Key、改配置 这个项目做了什么 TeamoRouter 是一个 LLM API 路由网关，把上面这些问题都封装到路由层解决。用户只需要一个 API Key，后端自动处理路由、负载均衡、协议兼容。 技术亮点 1. 完整的 Agent 协议支持 与市面上常见的 HTTP-only 中转不同，TeamoRouter 完整支持 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的 Agent 协议栈： Tool Use / Function Calling SSE Streaming MCP (Model Context Protocol) Beta Features（如 Claude 的 computer use） 并行工具调用 这意味着 Claude Code 的 \---dangerously-skip-permissions\、Codex 的 Agent 模式等高级功能都能正常工作。 2. 从 ccswitch 迁移只需改一个环境变量 bash Before（ccswitch） export ANTHROPICBASEURL= After（TeamoRouter） export ANTHROPICBASEURL= export ANTHROPICAPIKEY=tr-xxxxxxxx 3. 多模型统一路由 bash 同一个 Key，调不同模型 export ANTHROPICBASEURL= export OPENAIBASEURL= 定价模式 按量后付费，约官方 API 价格的 10% 起，无月费无最低消费，支持国内支付渠道。适合个人开发者按需使用，也适合团队统一管理 API 支出。 Teamo Switch 配套的桌面客户端（macOS/Windows），可一键安装 Codex Desktop + 配置路由，不需要手动设置环境变量和代理。

projects.title: 一个新颖的【久坐提醒】app
projects.author: wangluowanglei
projects.summary: 🪑 久坐提醒 - Stand Up Reminder 不止是"定时响一下"，而是一个会记住你久坐欠债、用科学剂量帮你还清的健康伙伴。 一款基于科学健康模型的久坐提醒 App。它不靠简单的倒计时闹钟，而是用一套"有效久坐分 + 起身抵消"的算法，把你的久坐风险实时量化成颜色，并用双气泡可视化让你一眼看懂身体状态。 ✨ 核心特点 1. 颜色会"记忆"久坐欠债，不是一坐到点就响 整屏背景色随有效久坐分实时渐变：绿 → 黄 → 红 → 深红。坐越久越红，且起身后颜色不会瞬间变绿，而是随你站立时长逐步回落——直观表达"健康债要慢慢还"。 2. 起身抵消有科学剂量，不是"站一下就清零" 恢复模型基于哥伦比亚大学 2023 年随机交叉试验：每坐 30 分钟 + 起身轻走 5 分钟，可使餐后血糖峰值降低约 58%。 所以 App 里起身 1 分钟不够（颜色仍偏黄），站够 5 分钟才算一次"有效休息"，颜色才回到绿色。让你做"有效"的起身，而不是敷衍地站一下。 3. 双气泡可视化，一眼看懂"坐 vs 起身" 🔴 坐气泡：随久坐时长变大，到警告阈值后开始裂开（最多 6 条裂纹），直观警示"快撑不住了"。 🟢 起身气泡：随站立时长变大，代表恢复进度，站够最佳休息时间就圆满。 4. 真后台提醒，杀掉 App 也能提醒 基于本地通知预调度 + 墙钟时间补算： 切后台被系统冻结的计时，回前台按真实时间自动补齐（不会出现"后台 5 分钟计时却没动"）。 即使锁屏、App 被系统回收，到点照样响铃 + 震动。 后台提醒数量做了收敛，避免 App 被杀后"连环轰炸"。 5. 高度可配置，适配你的节奏 提醒阈值、警告阈值、重复/稍后间隔、有效起身时长、提醒方式（铃声 / 震动 / 屏幕闪动，可任意叠加）——全部可在设置页自定义并持久化。 🆚 和传统久坐提醒 App 的差别 | 维度 | 传统久坐提醒 App | 本 App | |------|------------------|--------| | 提醒逻辑 | 固定倒计时，到点响铃 | 有效久坐分实时量化风险，颜色渐变反馈 | | 起身判定 | 点一下"我起来了"就清零 | 按科学剂量抵消，站够时长才算有效休息 | | 状态反馈 | 一个数字 / 一句提示 | 整屏颜色 + 双气泡 + 裂纹，多维直观 | | 科学依据 | 多为经验设定 | 基于哥大 2023 RCT 临床研究的恢复速率 | | 久坐"记忆" | 起身即归零，无连续性 | 颜色有记忆，逐步回落，符合身体真实恢复 | | 后台可靠性 | 切后台常常不准/不响 | 墙钟补算 + 本地通知，后台/锁屏/被杀仍提醒 | | 可配置性 | 通常只能改提醒间隔 | 阈值/间隔/恢复目标/提醒方式全可调 | | 数据与 AI | 多为孤立提醒 | 会话数据可上报，预留 AI 趋势分析与健康建议 | 🧬 一句话总结 传统 App 把久坐当成"定时任务"，到点提醒你； 这款 App 把久坐当成"健康账户"，实时算出你的健康欠债，并用科学剂量引导你真正还清。 1、在app store里搜索 久坐提醒 - stand up reminder 2、正常时间内的界面 3、超出时间的界面 4、急需起身的界面

projects.title: Show HN: Decomp Academy – Learn to decompile GameCube games into matching C
projects.author: jackpriceburns
projects.summary: Over the past few months I've been heavily involved in the decompilation community. I've been hands-on decompiling a beloved game from my childhood (Star Fox Adventures). I started this journey with zero prior decomp experience—and to make things worse I had never really touched C nor assembly either. Learning how to decompile was challenging. It's difficult to find any good learning resources for it and any open-source projects for this are inactive and/or contain little actual learning material. So I put together Decomp Academy! Decomp Academy is an interactive way to learn how to decompile PowerPC assembly back into C. The site runs a live Metrowerks CodeWarrior GC/2.0 compiler, converts your C into assembly, and then checks how close your assembly matches the target. If even 1 instruction or bit is off, that's a fail. This is the gold standard for video game decompilation and this is much stricter than a normal decompile. As of writing there are 250+ lessons on the site and the lessons start at the very basics so anyone with a little programming experience should be able to jump straight in, even if you're not a C expert. Some lessons also have real functions taken from live open source decomp projects (Star Fox Adventures, Mario Party 4, Pikmin, Metroid Prime). The idea being you learn everything you need to know to be able to jump in and contribute to a real decompilation project when done. The site is completely free, open source and you have access to all lessons without having to sign up. All lessons are stored in markdown in the repo (src/curriculum), it's trivial to add or modify lessons. The site is very new and the lessons are rapidly changing every day with a whole C++ section on the way. The site has already been well received by the decomp community and I'm happy to share it with HN. I'm very keen on others to contribute to this project and I hope this becomes the best resource on the internet for learning the art of decompilation. Please let me know what you think! Source: https://github.com/JackPriceBurns/decomp-academy-fe

projects.summary: Nada is the easiest way to turn your voice into music. Hum, sing, or whistle an idea, and instantly convert it into MIDI. Arrange your melodies on mobile, choose from a variety of instruments, and build songs wherever inspiration strikes. No AI generation involved, just your own creativity, captured faster.

projects.title: VoxisLive
projects.summary: Voxis Live listens to anything on your Windows PC — videos, games, calls — and speaks a live translation back in your language, a couple seconds behind. 79 languages, two-way meeting mode, and an open-source bring-your-own-key build with zero telemetry.

projects.title: attentional fatigue
projects.summary: Brain training grounded in cognitive science. 5 core games × 20 difficulty levels. 5 minutes a day to sharpen your mind. BrainGymG is a science-based brain training app designed to improve your core cognitive abilities through short, engaging daily sessions. Built around five classic cognitive science paradigms, each game targets a specific mental faculty
